name: Paradise Falls (Cheshunt)

facts.claim: Paradise Falls is a waterfall in Alpine National Park, about 20 minutes from Whitfield.
It is reached by a short 500 m walk and is best after rain.

name: Lake William Hovell

facts.claim: Lake William Hovell is a reservoir at the top of the King River valley, about 18 km from Cheshunt.
Visitors picnic and barbecue on the foreshore, fish, canoe and walk the shoreline.
It has a designated swimming area, and jet-skis and water-skiing are not allowed.

name: Dartmouth Dam

facts.claim: Dartmouth Dam is a 180 m high dam across the Mitta Mitta River in north-east Victoria, near Mount Bogong.
It is operated by Goulburn-Murray Water for the Murray-Darling Basin Authority and has a grassed picnic area, boat ramp, playground, fishing and camping.
It is the largest-capacity dam in Victoria.

name: Australian Alps Walking Track

facts.claim: The track runs about 650 km from Walhalla in Victoria to Tharwa near Canberra.
It follows ridges and high plains through Baw Baw, Alpine, Kosciuszko and Namadgi national parks and mostly avoids towns.
Many walkers do shorter sections such as the Baw Baw Plateau and the Bogong High Plains.

name: Murray to the Mountains Rail Trail

facts.claim: A sealed off-road cycling and walking trail from Wangaratta to Bright, with a branch to Beechworth.
The main route is about 95 km; a separate section links Rutherglen to Wahgunyah on the Murray.
It follows the route of the former Bright railway line.

name: Omeo

facts.claim: Omeo is a small town on the Great Alpine Road east of Mount Hotham, known as the City of the Alps.
Gold was found in Livingstone Creek in 1845 and many historic buildings remain.
Attractions include the Justice Precinct with its 1893 court house and the Oriental Claims gold diggings.
